title: Editorial: Generative AI in education
extended_summary:
This paper is an editorial introduction to a Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence special topic on generative AI in education. Rather than reporting a single empirical study, it frames the broader problem of how generative AI may reshape educational practice through personalized content generation, AI tutoring, assessment support, feedback generation, career mentoring, and other learner-facing applications. The editorial also highlights major concerns that accompany these opportunities, including answer accuracy, emotional quality of responses, interpretability, fairness, ethics, privacy, and the risk that AI systems may mislead or deceive learners.

The article’s main approach is to synthesize and briefly describe the 11 papers included in the research topic. These papers span several educational uses of generative AI, including large language model feedback, adolescents’ use of AI chatbots for schoolwork, critical thinking support, pre-service teacher use of ChatGPT for mathematical proofs, whole-learner modeling, personalized assessment, AI mentors for STEM career exploration, academic integrity, interactive listening assessment, deception detection with AI robots among Japanese middle school students, and a mini-review of generative AI for students’ cognitive and emotional needs. Across these summaries, the editorial emphasizes both promise and caution, especially the potential value of human-in-the-loop approaches.

No single participant sample or implementation context is studied directly in the editorial itself. Instead, it spans multiple educational contexts and populations discussed across the included papers, ranging from adolescents and middle school students to pre-service teachers and broader education stakeholders. Because it is an editorial, it does not provide a unified intervention duration, setting, or implementation protocol.

The main conclusion is that generative AI shows substantial potential to personalize learning, extend support beyond class hours, increase engagement, and enhance assessment and mentoring, but that these benefits depend on responsible and carefully designed integration. The editorial repeatedly points to unresolved challenges involving accuracy, emotional appropriateness, interpretability, fairness, privacy, ethical use, and deceptive or harmful outputs. It suggests that future progress will require more rigorous research and thoughtful use of human oversight to ensure that generative AI augments rather than undermines educational practice.
quality_tier_rationale: This article is an editorial that summarizes a special issue rather than reporting a primary empirical study or systematic synthesis with extractable methods and results. It provides narrative commentary on included papers but no standalone evaluative methodology for causal or correlational inference.
impact_tier_rationale: The editorial itself does not estimate an intervention effect, so impact is unclear rather than directly demonstrated as positive or negative. It points to possible benefits and risks of generative AI in education, but these are descriptive summaries without pooled or directly measured impacts.

interventions.use_case: Editorial overview of generative AI chatbots, tutors, and conversational agents used for personalized instruction, feedback, schoolwork support, assessment, and mentoring across the papers in the special issue.
Summarizes included papers on LLM-generated feedback and AI-supported assessment item/task generation, including automated feedback applications in education.
Discusses included work on AI-enhanced robots interacting with students, including deception and incorrect-information risks in educational settings.
